If you're looking for specific help, could you give a few details? Age, sex, what's causing the depression (general ideas or specific, both work).

My approach is different depending on who it is. What I can offer is this: don't tell them to smile, don't tell them they'll get over it, and don't tell them they just need to "think happy thoughts" or anything along those lines.

I know for me personally, those are the worst things to hear when I'm depressed. I will immediately disregard the person & will no longer open up to them.

See if you can get them involved in activities for you. Ask them for assistance with something, ask them to take a ride with ya cause you need opinions on clothes/games/whatever, ask them to be a sounding board for a problem/idea. Give them a cause, and let them know they're useful and important.

Listen when they need to talk. Sit there when they need company. Drag them out when they need sunshine.

It's a fine balance between offering support and forcing action for their benefit.

I also suffer from depression and I agree with everything you said. I often don't want to go out and do things and I really resent it if people are too forceful. I know they mean well, so I try not to hold it against them, but it makes me want to avoid talking to them in general.

Sometimes I do want to talk about those types of things, but I'll bring it up, and never in the overly optimistic way of thinking I just need "think more positively".

It's often a horrible double-edged sword for me: I want people around to try and help me out of it, but then I don't want to go anywhere or do anything because what's the point?

Talking is sometimes the best thing to do but it can feel like the worst. You worry if people understand where you're coming from, you worry that you sound like you're whining, you worry that you won't be taken seriously. The hardest part for us when depressed sometimes is simply addressing it out loud to someone.
